why_angle: ThrottleBuff and MotorcycleGPSHub list wired screens only and say no more than that the AIO-5 Lite 'needs a power connection'. Neither says which screens can move between bikes or how: the F5 runs on its own battery, the AIO-5 Play takes a $9 USB cable, and the Lite and AIO-6 must be wired to the battery. Neither prices a second-bike setup, and neither warns that the 'Portable' W702 Plus burns out on USB-C power. This page now has all of that.

page.answer: Short answer. The best portable wireless CarPlay screen for a motorcycle is the Aoocci F5: a built-in battery gives about 10 h of use per charge, so it moves between bikes with no wiring. Chigee's AIO-5 Lite must be hardwired; Carpuride's W502 needs 12 V or 11.25 W USB.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Total cost with a second bike: Aoocci F5: $189 + $16 clamp = $205. Chigee AIO-5 Play: $399.99 + $9 USB adapter cable = $408.99, plus a mount. Carpuride W702/W502/W619: $269.99 + $29.99 U-bracket = $299.98, plus a USB port or harness on that bike. Chigee AIO-6: $499 + $135 module + $175 second-bike kit = $809, with battery wiring on both bikes.
  • USB power the Carpuride needs: 4.5 V × 2.5 A = 11.25 W minimum from the port. On the harness it takes 12 V × 1 A = 12 W.
  • F5 days per charge: at 4 h of riding a day, 10 h ÷ 4 h = 2.5 days. The 10 h figure is Aoocci's own rating.
  • Brightness is not what the extra money buys: Chigee rates the AIO-5 Play and Lite at 1,000 nits (1,200 nits peak), and Carpuride rates the W702/W502/W619 at 1,000 nits. That is a 1,000 − 1,000 = 0-nit gap on rated brightness. The Aoocci C3 (from $159.00) is 800 nits and IP67, which is 80% of that. Aoocci's 12 V power-bank cable lists the C3 Pro and C3 Plus as compatible, but not the plain C3.
  • AIO-5 Lite over the Play: $598.00 − $399.99 = $198.01 more, which buys front and rear Sony IMX307 cameras and a hardwired install.

How each screen is powered, and what that means for moving it

Aoocci F5. This is the only screen here with a built-in battery. Aoocci lists a 5.5-inch 1440 × 720 IPS display and about 10 hours of active use per charge. To use it on another bike you only need a second $16 ball-head clamp.

Chigee AIO-5 Play. Chigee's comparison table lists 'Power cable or USB cable' for the Play and 'Hardwired (Battery + ACC wire)' for the Lite. Chigee's $9 USB adapter cable (about 30 cm) is sold so you can 'use the same device across different bikes'. The Play's audible anti-theft alarm works only on the power cable. Chigee's comparison page showed the Play out of stock while its store listed it as available, so check stock before you order.

Carpuride W702/W502/W619. Carpuride's spec is 12 V at 1 A from the battery, or a USB cable that delivers more than 4.5 V at 2.5 A. When it is hardwired, Carpuride says to hold the power button to shut the unit down before you switch off the bike. Carpuride does not support HarmonyOS phones or Huawei P and Mate series phones. It says most phones on Android 11 or later are generally compatible.

Chigee AIO-6. The CG Quick-Release Module 'requires a direct power connection to your motorcycle's battery… USB power sources are not supported.' Each extra bike needs the $175 second-motorcycle kit, which comes with a power cable and Electro-Tap connectors.

The phone still needs power. Chigee explains that wireless CarPlay keeps the phone holding a Wi-Fi Direct link and encoding video in real time, and calls this 'the single largest variable affecting power consumption'. The F5's battery runs the screen, but nothing on a bike without wiring charges the phone. On long days, carry a pocket power bank such as {buy:anker-nano-power-bank-10k-45w-a1638} or fit a USB port.

Not recommended

Carpuride W702 Plus / W702S Plus for a portable setup. The name says 'Portable', but Carpuride's power warning says the USB-C port does not supply power and is for factory debugging only. It also warns that putting more than 5 V into it 'will cause the device to burn out'. The unit has to be wired to the battery through ACC on every bike you use it on.
